name: kanal
verdict_reason: In its own 2025 chart, kanal leads most sequential, MPSC and MPMC tests, including against std::sync::mpsc on a current toolchain. It does not lead everywhere: crossbeam-channel and std::sync::mpsc are ahead in some bounded SPSC tests. All numbers are chart-only and first-party.
tier_reason: Public benchmark code with machine, rustc and OS stated, but the results are only a chart image.
claimed_speedup: Chart only: messages per second in seq, SPSC, MPSC and MPMC tests (AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, rustc 1.85.1, Mar 19, 2025); no numbers in text.
workload: fereidani/rust-channel-benchmarks: seq, SPSC, MPSC and MPMC over bounded (size 0, 1, N) and unbounded channels with empty, usize and 8-pointer-sized messages; sync and async variants; compared with crossbeam-channel, std::mpsc, flume, async-channel, futures-channel and Go.
one_liner: MPMC channel with sync and async APIs that leads most of its own 2025 charts against std mpsc and crossbeam, though not bounded SPSC.
how_it_is_fast: Messages no larger than a pointer are encoded into the pointer itself; larger ones are copied directly from the sender's stack to the receiver's, as Go does, so bounded(0) channels need no heap allocation. Channel state sits behind a short, specially tuned mutex whose hold time is predictable.
use_it_when: MPSC or MPMC traffic where its chart shows the largest lead
Mixing sync and async endpoints on one channel
skip_it_when: Bounded single-producer single-consumer pipelines, where crossbeam-channel and std::sync::mpsc lead parts of its own chart
Code that cannot accept unsafe stack-to-stack copying in a dependency
caveats: Chart image only; no numbers in text.
First-party benchmark, one machine, no independent rerun found.
Async results run inside Tokio and are not directly comparable with the thread-based sync tests, as the README itself notes.
tradeoffs: Relies on unsafe direct memory copies between stacks.

evidence.quote: The fast sync and async channel that Rust deserves!
Results are based on how many messages can be passed in each scenario per second.
utilizing direct memory access to copy objects from the sender's stack or write directly to the receiver's stack
